angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,302,350 km at 18.02 pc = 0.97 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: distance 18.021 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 18.021 +/- 0.054 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
radiusSource: Radius 1.872 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: radius 1.872 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 22.456 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.088) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,302,350 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 9191 +/- 421 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: effective temperature 9191 +/- 421 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.034) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: effective temperature 9191 +/- 421 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.034) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * iot Cen: spectral type kA1.5hA3mA3Va (2006AJ....132..161G)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * iot Cen: projected rotation speed 85 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 172 (BS 5028)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
